purpose: Mechanistic pilot only: test whether purified opening boundary reduces preceding-image sensitivity while preserving sensitivity to target image content. No accuracy or novelty claim.
data: First 8 Mantis rows; retain first two images; replace one image with next row's corresponding image resized to identical dimensions; original benchmark questions not used.
prompt: What is the main subject in the second image? Answer with only a short noun phrase.
measurements: normalized boundary/target-patch-mean/query representation cosine drift across layers
limitations: Image resizing and prompt are synthetic diagnostic choices
Invariance alone does not prove correctness
Canonical end is a destructive-content control, not a proposed method
No evidence that canonicalization is novel or competitive yet
decision: Do not advance canonical boundary method solely from attention plots or an invariance gain. Require preservation of target sensitivity and actual benchmark benefit.
